meta.title: Kodak Invented the Digital Camera. Then Sat On It.
meta.hook: Kodak built the first self-contained digital-camera prototype in nineteen seventy-five, decades before digital photography took over.
meta.description: Kodak engineer Steven Sasson built the first working digital camera prototype in 1975 and Kodak patented the invention in 1978 — but did not bring it to market. Kodak filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in January 2012, years after rivals built the digital camera industry the company had invented first.

scenes.narration: Kodak built the first self-contained digital-camera prototype in nineteen seventy-five, decades before digital photography took over.

visual.visual_intent: A vintage bulky camera prototype on a workbench, archival warm light, close macro
visual.decision_reason: hook beat: the irony stated upfront

scenes.narration: Engineer Steven Sasson combined a charge-coupled device, digital memory, and cassette storage into an eight-pound experimental camera.

visual.visual_intent: An engineer's workbench with circuit boards and wires, archival 1970s style lighting

scenes.narration: It captured a low-resolution black-and-white image and needed seconds to record it, but the core idea worked.

visual.query: old bulky electronic device hands holding
visual.visual_intent: Hands holding a bulky, heavy prototype device, close focus, archival tone
visual.decision_reason: documented prototype specifications, National Inventors Hall of Fame / PetaPixel sourced

scenes.narration: Kodak continued developing digital technology, yet its economics remained deeply tied to film, processing, and photographic paper.

visual.visual_intent: A filing cabinet drawer with documents inside, dim office light, symbolic of shelving

scenes.narration: As digital cameras improved, every photo taken without film weakened the recurring business Kodak had dominated.

visual.visual_intent: Stacked rolls of photographic film, warm light, product-style still
visual.decision_reason: the commonly cited motive, marked probable — the full internal reasoning is more nuanced per historical fact-checks

scenes.narration: Kodak did sell digital products, but it could not replace the profits disappearing from its old model.

visual.visual_intent: A row of modern digital cameras on a store display, bright even light
visual.decision_reason: market outcome: competitors captured the digital camera industry

scenes.narration: The company filed for Chapter Eleven in twenty twelve. Inventing a transition is not the same as surviving it.

visual.query: old kodak film boxes fading archival
visual.visual_intent: Faded old Kodak film boxes on a dusty shelf, muted color, documentary tone
visual.decision_reason: Kodak Chapter 11 filing Jan 19 2012, closing payoff and CTA
